prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a steep downward viewpoint from an elevated brick structure, separating the scene into the foreground mortar pan (bright white, ~0.4–0.7 m away in the lower-left), the narrow brick wall crest running diagonally through the middle (~0.7–1.2 m away), a brick-strewn trench to the left of the wall (~1.5–2.2 m below), and the sunlit ground far below to the right (near-black, ~3–5 m down). Within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.4–0.9 m) are the mortar pan, the handheld trowel, and the top edge of the wall, while in frame 2 a taller wall on the far left (~0.5–1.0 m) and another person's gloved left hand (~0.6 m, about 0.4 m left of the pan) briefly enter the left edge of the view before retreating out of frame. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's right hand and trowel move from inside the pan (~0.5 m in frames 1–2) forward and right to spread mortar along the wall top (~0.8–1.0 m in frames 3 and 5), returning to scoop from the pan in frame 4 while the wearer's lower torso and leg (~0.4–0.6 m) appear at the bottom edge in frames 3 and 5. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map makes the multi-meter vertical drop between the wall top, the left-hand brick trench, and the lower ground on the right immediately obvious despite similar earthy colors and harsh shadows. However, the depth map is unreliable along the thin rebar rods protruding from the wall in frame 5 (which blend into the dark background) and inside the mortar pan where the concave interior and scooped mortar mound are flattened into a nearly uniform bright blob.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few foreground elements against an unsegmented black background: the round mortar pan (labeled 'bowl' in green) in the lower-left at ~0.4–0.7 m and parts of the camera wearer's own body (labeled 'person') at ~0.3–0.9 m in the lower-right of frames 4 and 5. In frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, the pan is partially occluded along its left and bottom edges by the frame boundary and along its lower-right rim by the wearer's hand in frame 4 (~0.5 m away, touching the pan) and torso/leg in frame 5 (~0.4 m away, immediately adjacent to the pan). Across the sequence, the segmented pan shifts from the bottom-left corner in frame 1, disappears entirely in frame 2 as the camera tilts left, and re-enters in frames 3–5 while the wearer's right hand moves from overlapping the pan in frame 4 to extending ~0.3 m right of the pan onto the wall in frame 5. The map usefully delineates the exact boundary between the wearer's hand or torso and the mortar pan in frames 4 and 5 where shadows and dark mortar obscure edges in RGB. However, it is highly unreliable overall: it completely misses the pan and both the wearer's hand and the second person's left hand in frame 2, fails to segment the brick walls, loose bricks, and trowel across all frames, and erroneously splits the camera wearer's leg/torso and right arm into two separate 'person' instances in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank (solid black) across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons despite body parts being visible in the RGB strip. In the RGB frames, the camera wearer looks steeply downward toward the mortar pan (~0.4–0.7 m in front and below) and the brick wall top (~0.7–1.2 m in front and to the right), keeping their right hand and forearm within arm's reach (~0.4–0.9 m) across all five frames as it alternates between scooping mortar in the pan (frames 1, 2, and 4) and applying it to the wall (frames 3 and 5). A second person stands mostly out of view to the left in frame 2, extending only an orange-gloved left hand (~0.6 m from the camera wearer and ~0.4 m left of the pan) into the left margin, while the camera wearer's red-shirted torso, blue-jeaned right leg, and sandal appear at the bottom edge (~0.3–0.8 m below the camera) in frames 3 and 5. Because no keypoints are detected, this map adds no spatial information beyond the RGB image and cannot indicate body orientation or gaze direction on its own. It is completely unreliable here due to extreme egocentric self-occlusion, steep downward viewing angles, and mortar-covered hands that prevent the pose estimator from recognizing truncated limbs and hands at the frame borders.
